panel.finding: The ranking's ORDER held, but its MAGNITUDE did not. On 20 fresh endpoint pairs none of which they used, lazysp_alternate certified 14/20 and q2c_nomodel 14/20, against 13/20 for q2c, collective_shared and collective_isolated - the same ordering as their headline (lazysp = q2c_nomodel > q2c = both collectives), with zero false certificates for every policy. But LazySP's entire margin over q2c is ONE pair, VFVS->ILSG, and it is again a VFVS-start, top-variant-target pair: on the 14 pairs that do not start from VFVS, all five policies resolve exactly the same set, and no pair was resolved by LazySP alone. So the advantage is narrow and structurally concentrated, not broad, exactly as our recount of their own panel found (all 18 of their LazySP-only wins are VFVS-start: 17 VFVS->ALKG plus 1 VFVS->AIKG). The 18-point headline gap is largely a composition effect - 80 of their 100 episodes start from VFVS, versus 6 of my 20 - so on a panel that does not oversample that one family the gap shrinks to 5 points (1 pair). Two further points cut against the headline reading: q2c_nomodel ties LazySP at 14/20, so the GP surrogate is not what buys the win, and LazySP is strictly the least assay-efficient policy on this panel (mean 352.6 assays over its resolved episodes versus 149.2 for q2c), spending more assays than q2c on every single pair both resolved.

items.title: The gja5a fin-length link, withdrawn
items.body: Offered as a second tie to the bioelectric fin-size story. It does not hold: the zebrafish fin-length connexin is gja1b, gja5a has no ZFIN fin record, and Daane’s own text puts cx43 under constrained, not accelerated, evolution.

items.title: The flying-fish genome claim, wrong
items.body: We said almost no molecular data exists for flying fish. An annotated genome does exist, and the error was load-bearing: it was repeated on every number in the map.
items.who: the project lead, not the thread that published it

items.title: A declared null, withdrawn
items.body: We published that no ray-to-interray signalling could be sourced in any fin of any fish. 3 papers contradict it, 1 of them already cited by the same thread on a title-only read. A title-only read was allowed to carry a universal negative; what survives is narrower and none of it pectoral.
items.who: our own curation pass, not the thread that wrote it

items.title: An overstated “settled”, withdrawn
items.body: We said lat4a’s identity was settled on three records. Which gene carries the allele IS resolved to slc43a2a, on the paper’s own chromosome-15 mapping and ZFIN’s allele assignment. Which paralogue carries the flying-fish signal is not: in the paper’s own data both are accelerated, the other more strongly.

designval.definingAxisWhy: TWO independent reasons, on opposite sides: the baseline has no value and the design has only a figure. This is the axis the whole design claim is about.
designval.phenotypicVerdict: NOT CLOSE, and largely UNSHOWN. 9 of 10 axes cannot be scored. The single scoreable axis scores FAIL at f = 0.00. The axis the entire design claim rests on (pectoral fin length / SL) cannot be scored, and for two independent reasons at once.
designval.consequence: The claim that we can DESIGN an organism is not supported by this validation, and the reason is not that the design scored badly: it is that the design is not measurable on the axes that define it, and the one genetic number that can be computed (1/74) says the design reproduces a single convergent locus out of everything known to differ. Dropping the claim outright under rule 1 overstates what this gate can tell us; the honest position is PREREG rule 2, drop the claim as UNSUPPORTED.

threads.title: Swarm vs single-agent comparison
threads.headline: Two pre-registered experiments, same 4 arms, 20 claims each, equal model and budget. Experiment 1 (plans from memory): centralized swarm 19, decentralized 18 (1 fabricated id), isolated 17, single agent 13; replicate ordering identical. Experiment 2 (web fetch required, hard cap): centralized 18, decentralized 17, isolated 16, single 12, zero fabricated ids everywhere, ordering as predicted beforehand. The centralized swarm beats the single agent and the isolated workers in both; the single agent costs about a tenth as much. Three findings drafted as Project Delphi nanopubs (unsigned, unpublished; np check passes) in swarm/nanopubs/.

threads.title: Lean formalization
threads.headline: Lean 4, 0 sorry, standard axioms: eight claims (Kimura k = mu and fixation probability, Fisher FTNS, Maynard Smith twofold cost, Thompson's cube law, flight power ch02-06, the size limit for flight ch02-07, speed proportional to the square root of size ch02-10) and five extensions (favored fixation floor, blueprint well-formedness, area law, strength law, bending law) (fixation >= i/M when selection does not oppose a mutant; well-formedness of a generated anatomical blueprint). 92 theorems, 53 lemmas; 26 of 26 statement or data mutants rejected, 11/11 controls. NEW: a kernel-checked certificate for the organism thread's flying-fish blueprint: 536 distinct terms, 674 part_of edges, acyclic, every term reaches the body root, 1390 never_in_taxon and 5435 in_taxon statements pinned from Ubergraph exclude nothing, distinct counts per level body 1, organ_system 13, organ 67, tissue 198, cell 257 (the placement-vs-term count the organism thread fixed by hand). Structural only: it does not say the fish is real or the ontology right. Thompson's cube law has a formal statement (exact exponent 3) beside the claims thread's measured exponents (2.74-2.86 on age-bin means; 2.10 to 3.10 by age window). Flying-fish substitution budget still inconclusive. 33 unsigned nanopub drafts pass np check + parse + Delphi lint; no human named; nothing signed or published. Scaling laws R2-R9 from the physics thread are proved in lean/Delphi/Scaling.lean with every contested quantity a named hypothesis: strength and bending complete Galileo's square-cube argument, so 28 constraints rule; on the enumerator's 44 candidates the verdicts are 2 eliminated (both proposed-here), 19 consistent, 23 cannot-rule, and WP-077/C1 (leaf bending) is consistent under the body-like-load reading as the physics thread predicted; nothing in the square-cube rows is eliminated because they restate the laws. Illustrative eliminations: a giant claimed to stand, a glider below its minimum speed, a constant-thickness leaf that still claims a bending limit. AUDIT (Amit's direction): every one of the 92 theorems checked against the real flying fish (lean/AUDIT-FLYING-FISH.md): 19 hold when instantiated (the blueprint certificate, the exact minimum-speed bound on the Park and Choi specimen with v_min 9.85 m/s against field speeds 10-20 m/s, the cube law approximately at Davenport's 2.981), 6 have their isometry hypotheses violated by measured within-species exponents (fin area 1.834, wing loading 1.236), 67 cannot be evaluated for want of a named input (no mutation rate, fixation probability, fitness variance, material strength, muscle power or second body size is measured for Exocoetidae). Morphology grounding for all 110 pieces of the 3D model (lean/morphology-grounding.json): wing size is bounded by the minimum-speed theorem (lifting area needed 0.0123 m^2 at 10 m/s against 0.0127 m^2 measured), fin rays and skeleton reach the strength and bending lemmas with inputs missing, organs are grounded only structurally through the certified blueprint, and eyes and the dorsal and anal fins are reached by no theorem. FLIGHT (hub items 3-5): lean/Delphi/Flight.lean adds general allometry with measured exponents, the climb bound, the steady-glide range with ground effect, and the oxygen-to-power bound (Fick) composed with the power required, replacing the bare muscle premise with a crossover size limit; 32 constraints, 111 theorems. The glide bound fires on the real fish: one unpowered glide from 8 m with the measured L/D 4.37 reaches at most 35 m (40.7 m with the measured 14% ground effect) against field glides of 50 m, so the single-glide reading is eliminated and taxiing thrust or a higher L/D must enter the model. Physics' hypothetical flier: 7 m/s consistent, 4 m/s eliminated with a kernel-accepted certificate, real fish at 15 m/s consistent; its 1 m/s climb needs Q·Ca ≥ 0.927 ml O2/s (927 ml/min/kg), no Exocoetidae physiology to compare. lean/eliminate/browser-check.mjs (generated from constraints.json, dependency-free, environment from conditions/baseline.json) lets the Design Studio evaluate the same formulas in the browser; not a kernel check, and it says so on every result. PHYSIOLOGY vs FLIGHT: C14 instantiated with the physiology chain's own proxies for a 0.06 kg fish (cardiac output 0.0656 ml/s from cardiac.js, arterial O2 content 0.187 ml/ml from haemoglobin.js at the chain's arterial saturation, efficiency 0.15 and 19.34 J/ml from muscle.js, each a labelled proxy from another teleost): the aerobic ceiling is 0.0357 W against 1.35 W for level flight at 10 m/s, so sustained aerobic flight is ruled out for the real fish, for the hypothetical flier at 7 m/s, and at the minimum speed itself, each with a kernel-accepted certificate, by a factor of about 40 at the most generous lift-to-drag ratio. The elimination rests on the proxies, not on flying-fish physiology; what the fish does is glide and burst on white-muscle stores, which the theorem does not bound. GENOTYPE (hub direction A): five genotype-level checks are proved in lean/Delphi/Genotype.lean and two physiology bounds in lean/Delphi/Physiology.lean, so 42 constraints now rule. The genetic code is a 64-codon table the kernel evaluates: a claimed amino-acid change below the code distance is impossible, which clears the project's own slc43a2a F326L variant (phenylalanine to leucine in one substitution, UUU to UUA) and eliminates a control claiming the same change in none, and methionine to tryptophan in one. Pleiotropy closure: an edit shown as changing one structure is eliminated when the map links the gene further, which fires on tbx5a (8 linked nodes in the fin subtree) and passes kcnk5b (the map links it to the pectoral fin alone there). Developmental ordering: 8 develops_from edges of the fin subtree are certified by a kernel evaluation of the checker on the recorded ZFIN stages, 4 more have an unknown stage and are NOT certified; a claim putting the fin before its fin bud is eliminated. Substitution time and Haldane's cost are stated honestly: the time bound eliminates a control of 100 substitutions in 5 generations but nothing about a wing, because no required substitution count for a wing is defined anywhere in this project, and Haldane's accounting is carried as a named hypothesis the modules never prove. Of 10 genotype candidates 5 are eliminated and 4 consistent, with 6 of the eliminations kernel-checked. ALTITUDE (hub part B): lean/Delphi/Altitude.lean proves that in any atmosphere where density and oxygen partial pressure fall with height, the minimum speed and the power to fly at it rise while the aerobic supply falls, so flight possible at a height is possible at every lower one, infeasibility propagates upward (a ceiling in that sense), and a design that cannot fly at the ground cannot fly at any height. The direction is proved; the SIZE is data and it is gentle (about 30 percent more required capacity from 0 to 5000 m), and the real fish sits more than thirty times below every boundary at every height, so the shrink with altitude is not the reason it cannot fly high: the reason is the oxygen budget at sea level. The physics thread's truly-flying-fish v2 at 1000 m, translated into this checker's names (lean/eliminate/tff-candidates.json), gives 1 consistent and 2 eliminated, both kernel-checked: cruise at 6 m/s is consistent, 4 m/s is below the minimum speed, and the aerobic ceiling of 0.0358 W at that altitude is eliminated against 1.87 W required. Air density at altitude is the physics thread's NASA Glenn troposphere fit and an explicit design parameter; the conditions file stays at sea level. OBSERVATIONS AS HYPOTHESES, NOT AXIOMS (hub, from Amit): lean/Delphi/Empirical.lean adds the project's own measurements as Lean structures whose fields are the numbers and whose proof obligations are the inequalities, and declares NO axiom: #print axioms still reports only propext, Classical.choice and Quot.sound for every theorem, the witness included. 6 observations (isometry fails within a species; the fitted mass-exponent band; the measured teleost aerobic ranges; no gill ventilation in air; the measured fin-ratio range; lethality before the scoring stage), 1 project convention (required-for is never propagated down part-of), and one entry left OUT because it is already a theorem (a part cannot appear before its precursor). Four of them rule: 9 candidates give 5 eliminated and 4 consistent, all 5 eliminations kernel-checked and each reported as CONDITIONAL on the observation it rests on (E2, E3, E4, E7), so a reader may reject an observation and drop that elimination alone. The one that matters: inside the measured teleost ranges the sustained aerobic ceiling at 0.06 kg is at most 0.0458 W, so the real fish's 1.3473 W of level flight is ruled out for EVERY teleost the record allows, not only for the particular proxies the chain commits. Non-vacuity: an inconsistent set of observations would let the checker eliminate everything and that failure would look like success, so Delphi.Empirical.measured instantiates every entry with the measured numbers at once and empirical_nonvacuous is the witness; two mutants attack it, one moving a band off the measured value and one making a contradictory pair, and both are rejected. The law catalogue (lean/LAWS.md, lean/laws.json) now lists 41 laws by level with their status, their Studio fields and their scope: 23 proved, 3 resting on a named hypothesis, 6 empirical observations and 7 named as not formalised at all. The browser checker shows the empirical rows in their own band, each stating the observation a user could reject.

threads.title: Text-to-organism design
threads.headline: New assignment from the hub: sim-engine/, our own simulation backend as an MCP server, v1 runs with 5 tools and 21 passing tests. Its first pre-registered test FAILED and that is the result worth reporting: a single-morphogen threshold model predicts the WRONG AXIS for the hhip fin phenotype. Measured is dorsoventral +50 percent with anteroposterior unchanged; the model puts all its growth on the anteroposterior axis, because a ZPA drawn as a posterior strip spanning the bud height leaves no room to grow dorsoventrally. Nothing was tuned afterwards. The organism thread work is unchanged and still live: ten blueprints, 35 unsigned records.
